articles.headline: Scottie Barnes rallies Raptors to 125-118 win, handing Clippers their 6th straight defeat
articles.description: — Scottie Barnes scored 15 of his 22 points in the fourth quarter, Immanuel Quickley had 27 and the Toronto Raptors rallied for a 125-118 win over the skidding Los Angeles Clippers on Monday night.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Scottie Barnes scored 15 of his 22 points in the fourth quarter, Immanuel Quickley had 27 and the Toronto Raptors rallied for a 125-118 win over the skidding Los Angeles Clippers on Monday night.


              Toronto trailed by 13 going into the final period, but Barnes hit a turnaround jumper with 2:08 remaining to give the Raptors their first lead as part of a 12-1 run.


              RJ Barrett scored 26 for Toronto. Barnes also finished with 15 rebounds and eight assists.


              Kobe Sanders had a career-high 26 points for the Clippers, who have dropped six straight games since winning their season opener Oct. 21 against Sacramento.


              It was the second game of a back-to-back for both teams. The Clippers were coming off a 124-112 loss at Golden State on Sunday, while the Raptors fell 131-125 at the Los Angeles Lakers.


              The matchup lost some of its luster with Raptors forward Kawhi Leonard unavailable because of a left knee injury, delaying his return to Southern California after spending the previous seven seasons with the Clippers (he missed one due to injury). 


              His largely disappointing tenure ended when the Clippers had to forfeit five first-round draft picks and were fined $30 million for circumventing salary cap rules in regard to how Leonard was compensated. Team owner Steve Ballmer was suspended for one year.


              Leonard was traded back to Toronto in September for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round draft picks, two second-round picks and a pick swap nearly three months after the deal was originally agreed to in July. It had been delayed pending resolution of the NBA's investigation.


              Dick made his first start for the Clippers and had 12 points, four rebounds and three assists in 29 minutes.


              Clippers coach Tyronn Lue was on the floor despite an illness that prevented him from holding his pregame news conference. Lue had been called a game-time decision by a team spokesman.


              Up next
              Raptors: At Denver on Wednesday night.


              Clippers: Host Miami on Wednesday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Stephen Curry scores 34 points as Warriors hold off Suns 116-113 in testy game with three technicals
articles.description: — Stephen Curry had 34 points, seven assists and six rebounds, Charles Bassey scored a career-best 19 points to go with eight rebounds, and the Golden State Warriors held off the Phoenix Suns 116-113 in a testy matchup Monday night featuring three...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- — Stephen Curry had 34 points, seven assists and six rebounds, Charles Bassey scored a career-best 19 points to go with eight rebounds, and the Golden State Warriors held off the Phoenix Suns 116-113 in a testy matchup Monday night featuring three technicals and Draymond Green's ejection.


              Curry made 11 of 12 free throws, missing his final attempt with five seconds left. He made his initial 51 of the season.


              Devin Booker had 26 points and five assists for the Suns before fouling out with 58 seconds left. 


              Green was ejected two minutes into the third quarter for consecutive technical fouls. Khaman Maluach had pushed Green to the ground in the paint moments earlier and the Golden State star jumped up from beneath and wrapped his arms around the Suns center and threw him to the floor. Dillon Brooks immediately sprinted in to enter the fray and approached Green, and they pushed and shoved. Green put his hand on Brooks’ neck, and both received technicals.


              Tempers flared again with 7:26 remaining in the game as players put their hands on each other, separated by security personnel. Miles Bridges received a technical as “a physical escalator” when he ran to the baseline area and shoved Bassey after Bassey kept his arms wrapped around Jalen Green’s head when they fought for a rebound beneath the basket. 


              Brandin Podziemski added 20 points in the Warriors' fifth straight win after an 0-3 start, as Golden State reached the midway point in its six-game homestand.


              Bridges added 21 points and Brooks contributed 18 points, eight rebounds and four assists.


              After Booker's jumper put Phoenix ahead 55-39 with 3:47 left in the second quarter, the Warriors responded with a 12-0 burst and trailed 57-51 at intermission.


              Golden State used its seventh different starting lineup in eight games, with Will Richard making his second start of the season.


              Yaxel Lendeborg followed up his career-high 37 points from a night earlier in a 124-112 win against the Clippers with 16 points, five assists and five rebounds. Curry and Green had both rested Sunday.


              Up next
              
              Suns: Host Portland on Wednesday night.


              Warriors: Host Miami on Thursday night.

articles.headline: Caleb Williams and Jeffery Simmons lead the Bears past the Seahawks 34-17
articles.description: — Jeffery Simmons ran out of the tunnel for the first time since joining the Chicago Bears with a new uniform, orange sleeves and a wide smile as he welcomed the move that put right into contention...
articles.body:
SEATTLE -- — Jeffery Simmons ran out of the tunnel for the first time since joining the Chicago Bears with a new uniform, orange sleeves and a wide smile as he welcomed the move that put right into contention with important games on big stages.


              Then he delivered exactly what the Bears needed.


              Simmons had a sack in his Bears debut as part of a dominant defensive performance that helped lead Chicago to a 34-17 victory over the Seattle Seahawks 34-17 on Monday night.


              “When I attacked the field, I wasn’t worried about the trade,” Simmons said. “I wasn’t worried about all the outside noise. All I was worried about is play after play, just give the team everything I got.”


              Acquired last week from Tennessee for a package that included two first-round picks, Simmons took little time to make a big impact on a defense that had lacked difference-makers.


              He had a sack on the opening drive, added another tackle for loss and finished with six tackles, three pressures and a pass defensed with coach Ben Johnson describing his impact as “profound." Chicago held Seattle to 252 yards and one third-down conversion on 11 tries.


              “He has me up off of the bench,” receiver Rome Odunze said. “Watching them third downs, watching the defense in general to see what he’s going to do next. He brings the energy to them. Obviously, his play-making ability ignites the defense, ignites the offense, ignites the team as a whole.”


              Caleb Williams was extremely efficient for the Bears (6-2) against one of the NFL's stingiest defenses, committing no turnovers, taking just one sack and throwing for 247 yards while completing 71% of his passes.


              Williams' play helped set up three short touchdown runs by D'Andre Swift and that proved to be more than enough against Sam Darnold and the Seahawks (4-4), thanks to the impact Simmons had on the defense.


              “We knew it was going to be challenging and this was one of the more elaborate game plans in terms of what we were asking (Williams) to do as well,” Johnson said. “He stayed calm and collected throughout. I think that there are some times where it can get a little bit chaotic and yet he didn’t allow that to happen.” 


              The defending champion Seahawks lost for the third time in four games and are now looking up at the NFC playoff standings and can ill afford many more slip-ups. 


              The loss ended a 30-game streak for Seattle in the regular season and playoffs — the fourth longest for any team in the Super Bowl era — of not losing by more than four points.


              “We got beat. No other way to sugar coat it,” coach Mike Macdonald said. “When you look at the things that it takes to win in our league, we didn't do those things and they did.”

articles.headline: Jeffery Simmons, Bears' defense handle Seahawks
articles.description: Caleb Williams and Jeffery Simmons had the Bears controlling both sides of the ball on MNF.
articles.body:
SEATTLE -- From the moment Jeffery Simmons stepped onto the field Monday night, his impact provided the Chicago Bears an immediate return on their investment after trading two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder for the All-Pro defensive tackle last week.

The move signaled the Bears are all-in on contending for a Super Bowl, and it paid off quickly as they took down the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 34-17. It was their third straight win and fifth in their past six games.

Simmons elevated everyone around him on defense, and his impact was felt throughout. Seahawks QB Sam Darnold completed less than 50% of his passes with Simmons on the field and was a perfect 5-of-5 with a TD when he was off.

In consecutive games separated by 11 days, the Bears pulled off a franchise first, defeating the Super Bowl runner-up New England Patriots and then the defending champs in Seattle.

The Seahawks have lost three of their past four games.

Chicago Bears (6-2)

What to make of the quarterback performance: Right off the bat, Caleb Williams led the Bears on a 17-play, 80-yard touchdown drive, which was Chicago's longest opening drive since 2007 against the Packers. Williams used play-action passes, going 10-for-15 for 109 yards and a touchdown, the most completions and yards allowed by the Seahawks on play-action passes in a game this season. Seattle's defense entered Week 8 with the No. 1 pass defense in the NFL (144 yards allowed per game). Williams surpassed that mark by the two-minute warning in the first half and finished the game by completing 70.6% of his passes for 247 yards.

Most surprising performance: Credit the Simmons effect for injecting life into the Bears' ability to generate pressure with their defensive line in ways they couldn't the past two seasons, when they had a 25% pressure rate with a standard pass rush (four or fewer pass rushers). Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen didn't have to blitz as much as in previous games, and much of that can be credited to Simmons' presence. In 48 plays with Simmons on the field, the Seahawks' offense generated 146 yards (3.0 yards per play) and one touchdown to go along with three sacks and an interception. In eight plays with the All-Pro defensive tackle off the field, Seattle's offense had 106 yards and a touchdown and averaged 13.3 yards per play.

Stat to know: D'Andre Swift rushed 24 times for just 57 yards for a 2.4-yard average, but he ran for three touchdowns to boost his league-leading total to 10 (Buffalo's Josh Allen has nine). Swift is the first Bears player with 10 rushing TDs in a season since Raymont Harris had 10 in 1997. He is the first Bears player with 10 in the Bears' first eight games since Rick Casares had 11 in 1956.

articles.headline: Luka Doncic scores 42 points in another brilliant game, leading the Lakers past the Heat 138-117
articles.description: — Luka Doncic had 42 points, 13 assists and seven rebounds in another spectacular early-season performance, leading the Los Angeles Lakers to a 138-117 victory over the Miami Heat on Monday night.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — Luka Doncic had 42 points, 13 assists and seven rebounds in another spectacular early-season performance, leading the Los Angeles Lakers to a 138-117 victory over the Miami Heat on Monday night.


              Doncic scored at least 37 points in his fifth consecutive game, hitting six 3-pointers and showing off his playmaking skill just one night after he had 45 points and 15 assists in a win over Toronto.


              Austin Reaves scored 27 points and Walker Kessler added 15 points and 15 rebounds for the Lakers. Los Angeles is 6-2 after the fourth 40-point performance in his last five games from Doncic, who is averaging 43.4 points per game in that stretch.


              Giannis Antetokounmpo had 30 points, 12 rebounds and seven assists for the Heat, who opened a five-game West Coast trip with their fifth loss in seven games to begin the Greek superstar's debut season with Miami.


              Klay Thompson scored 19 points and Bam Adebayo had 16 for the Heat, who hadn't played since Friday.


              The Lakers also played Friday and then had to hold off the Raptors on Sunday night, but Doncic was still in his groove.


              Doncic began 16 points, five assists and four rebounds in yet another dominant first quarter. The defending NBA scoring champion is averaging 15.0 points in the opening period this season, scoring at least 13 in all but one of his seven games.


              He had 24 points by halftime, and Doncic got nine more in the first 4 1/2 minutes after the break to balloon the Lakers’ lead to 93-74. Miami never seriously threatened to close the gap down the stretch, with Reaves stepping up while Doncic rested to start the fourth quarter.


              Heat president Pat Riley got a big ovation from Lakers fans when he was shown on the scoreboard. The Lakers unveiled a statue of their Showtime era coach outside their downtown arena last season.


              Lakers forward Ziaire Williams returned from a three-game absence with a foot injury, but Jake LaRavia kept the starting spot previously held by Williams.


              Up next
              Heat: At Clippers on Wednesday night.


              Lakers: At Sacramento on Wednesday night.

articles.headline: Ravens QB Joe Fagnano (ankle) has chance to play Thursday, per Jesse Minter
articles.description: Ravens quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury but has "a chance" to play Thursday night, coach Jesse Minter said.
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- With the Baltimore Ravens' top three quarterbacks dealing with injuries, coach Jesse Minter was not definitive on who will be his starter for Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

In addition to Lamar Jackson (right thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) being ruled out for Thursday's game, the Ravens' No. 3 quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury.

"To Joe's credit, he's kind of fighting through a couple things he's dealing with," Minter said after Monday night's walk-through, "but expect him to have a chance to play on Thursday."

Fagnano was listed as a limited participant in Monday's walk-through practice.

Fagnano would become just the second undrafted rookie quarterback to start in the Ravens' 32-year history. The first undrafted rookie quarterback to start for Baltimore was Anthony Brown during the Ravens' 27-16 loss in the 2022 season finale at the Cincinnati Bengals.

The only healthy quarterback on the roster is Austin Reed, who was signed to the practice squad Monday. Reed, 26, has familiarity with the offensive system because he spent time at Ravens training camp this summer and also played under offensive coordinator Declan Doyle when they were both in Chicago last year.

Asked if the Ravens' quarterback situation is up in the air, Minter replied, "I think we'll figure that out over the next day or two."

Minter indicated that Baltimore could have a more definitive timetable on Jackson sometime this week. After Sunday's 36-10 loss at Buffalo, Minter said Jackson's injury "potentially" could be season-ending. Jackson, who will go on injured reserve, has not had surgery on his right thumb yet, according to Minter.

"I think when you lose a guy like Lamar, it's a little bit of every phase doing a little bit more," Minter said. "So, it's being able to play really good defense, being able to maybe make a play or steal a play on special teams, maybe a different style of offense of how we need to play."

Huntley, the Ravens' primary backup quarterback, will not play Thursday night, according to Minter. "We'll see how it goes from a long-term standpoint," Minter said.

The Ravens (4-4), who have lost three straight to fall into last place in the AFC North, are set to make a change at kicker. Minter said kicker Tyler Loop "potentially" might go on injured reserve because of a right groin injury.

"I would say [Loop was] dealing with something small that it kind of became a little bit more and leave it at that," Minter said.

Loop was listed as a nonparticipant in Monday's walk-through.

In his second season, Loop has struggled with consistency. He is 2-of-6 inside 50 yards, missing a 34-yard field goal attempt Sunday.

The Ravens have Jake Moody, a third-round pick in 2023 by the San Francisco 49ers, on the practice squad. Asked if Moody will kick Thursday, Minter said, "At this point, yes."

articles.headline: Moyes after 2nd Everton win over Newcastle: 'Not an easy thing'
articles.description: David Moyes hailed a "great result" for Everton as they secured back-to-back wins over Newcastle United with a 1-0 triumph at St James' Park on Monday.
articles.body:
David Moyes hailed a "great result" for Everton as they secured back-to-back wins over Newcastle United with a 1-0 triumph at St James' Park on Monday, calling it no easy feat.

Monday night's Premier League clash took place just four days after the Toffees claimed a 3-1 victory over the Magpies in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup and Moyes' side were able to secure three points on Tyneside.

A first half lacking in clear-cut chances from both sides saw Everton take the lead just four minutes after the restart when Tyrique George's low effort squeezed underneath Lukás Hornícek.

Thierno Barry then reacted quickly to pounce on the loose ball and stab home for his fourth league goal of the campaign.

Moyes said recording successive wins over the Magpies in such a short space of time was "not an easy thing," but was full of praise for his side's display as they claimed three points.

"They are so good in what they do as they give everything they've got," the Everton boss said.

"They're a brilliant group of players and they've had it tough as well. They want to keep winning and they've found it difficult with the way things have gone, but they're pulling it out and doing their best to be in all the games.

"It's never easy ... we beat Newcastle on Thursday night and to beat them again today is not an easy thing to do for any club and this level.

"To come here and get a good win tonight was a great result for us."

Victory ends a three-game winless run for Everton in the Premier League and sees them move into seventh in the standings, but Moyes was also pleased to earn a first away win in their league campaign.

He added: "We've actually done quite well in some of the games getting draws in difficult away games, but we've not picked up a victory and last season we had a great run of results away from home.

"So I was hoping to pick it up tonight and thankfully we did, clean sheet and got the goal that counted."

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle admitted his side need to "do things better" following a disappointing performance.

The Magpies struggled to threaten throughout the match and were frustrated further when Jacob Ramsey was dismissed with two yellow cards in quick succession at the death to leave the Tynesiders 13th in the table.

Asked what the solution is, Jaissle said: "We need to analyse that now in detail.

"It's also clear that I have the responsibility and I also take that as the manager of this club, and we need to do things better.

"There were many things there, not only in possession, which was not on the level we expected to see.

"Also out of possession, we wanted to press them high, we wanted to stretch them as soon as possible and make also a clear distinction if that was overplayed from their position that we defend in a compact block, but nothing between.

"Again, it was not much seen today on the pitch."

articles.headline: Jack Grealish, 'not match fit,' left out as Everton beat Newcastle again
articles.description: Jack Grealish was not named in Everton's squad for Monday's Premier League match at Newcastle United due to a fitness issue.
articles.body:
Jack Grealish was not named in Everton's squad for Monday's Premier League win over Newcastle United due to a fitness issue.

The 31-year-old was left out of the team for Thursday's Carabao Cup fourth-round meeting against the Magpies due to a breach of club discipline and Everton went on to win the game 3-1.

Both sides met again at St James' Park in the Premier League and Grealish was not included, with a starting lineup post on the Everton club website stating that he is "not match fit."

Everton went on to beat Newcastle for the second time in four days as Thierno Barry scored the game's only goal in a 1-0 win.

Grealish was also absent for the Toffees' 2-0 loss to Arsenal on Oct. 24, but that was put down to illness.

Providing an update on Grealish after the match, manager David Moyes said he is "not available yet."

Asked if there is a way back longer term, Moyes replied: "Of course there is, yeah."

The former Aston Villa midfielder is on a second consecutive season-long loan from Manchester City and has made six appearances for Everton this season.

During the last campaign, Grealish provided six assists and scored two goals in 20 appearances before suffering a season-ending foot injury in January.

He was not part of the England side that made a run to the semifinals of the World Cup before losing to Argentina.

Information from PA was used in this report.

articles.headline: Barry leads Everton to second win over Newcastle in four days
articles.description: Thierno Barry's second-half strike helped Everton return to winning ways in the Premier League with a 1-0 victory over Newcastle at St James' Park.
articles.headlineJa: バリーがリードし、エバートンが4日間で2度目のニューカッスル戦勝利を飾る
articles.descriptionJa: ティアノ・バリーが後半に決めたゴールにより、エバートンはセント・ジェームズ・パークでニューカッスルに1-0で勝利し、プレミアリーグで勝ち星を挙げた。
articles.body:
Thierno Barry's second-half strike helped Everton return to winning ways in the Premier League with a 1-0 victory over Newcastle United at St James' Park.

Following a first half lacking in clear-cut opportunities, the Toffees took the lead shortly after the restart when Barry stabbed home his fourth league goal of the campaign.

A frustrating night soured further for the Magpies as they finished the game with 10 men when substitute Jacob Ramsey was shown two yellow cards in quick succession at the death.

Everton ended a three-game winless run in the Premier League and moved up to seventh in the table, while Newcastle slipped to 13th.

Monday's match took place just four days after Everton's 3-1 win over Newcastle in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup and both sides made two changes to their starting XI as Anthony Elanga and Joelinton came in for the Magpies, while Jarrad Branthwaite and Harrison Armstrong lined up for the visitors.

Harvey Barnes looked lively on the left flank for the hosts, sending a curling shot wide before his looping cross floated narrowly past the far post and Jordan Pickford was forced to hold Will Osula's deflected cross from a tight angle.

Joelinton had an effort blocked by James Tarkowski and Merlin Röhl fired over the crossbar as both sides looked to break the deadlock.

James Garner blasted a free kick from the edge of the area straight into the Newcastle wall and Barnes was at the heart of the action again, firing in a dangerous cross which bounced off Branthwaite and was tipped over by Pickford.

Joelinton unleashed a fierce strike from distance which whizzed wide and Everton enjoyed a late flurry of chances before the break.

Jake O'Brien was unable to nod home Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's cross and Harrison Armstrong skewed a first-time effort wide.

The Toffees picked up where they left off only four minutes into the second half when a slick pass from a free kick set Tyrique George free on the left to fire low at Lukás Hornícek.

His shot squeezed underneath the Newcastle goalkeeper, but Barry was quick to react to tap in the loose ball and the goal stood following a VAR check for two close offside calls.

Branthwaite's header was tipped away by Hornicek as the visitors looked to quickly double their advantage, while Fabian Schär hooked an effort over the crossbar and Pickford held Joe Willock's header.

Hornicek was then called into action at the opposite end to push away Dewsbury-Hall's strike and the Magpies goalkeeper made a solid low save from the resulting corner to deny O'Brien.

Barnes' cross from the left was nearly turned in by Elanga at the far post, but the ball hit the post and trickled across the goal-line before being cleared.

Newcastle looked to threaten around the Everton box as Pickford punched away Jacob Murphy's corner and the ball was recycled back to Ramsey, who dragged his volley narrowly wide.

articles.headline: Kane says new Bayern deal 'extremely close,' will happen in coming days
articles.description: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is determined to help Bayern Munich come through more difficult moments as they prepare to face Atlético Madrid in the Champions League.
articles.headlineJa: ケイン、バイエルンとの新契約は「極めて近い」とし、近日中に締結へ
articles.descriptionJa: バロンドール受賞者のハリー・ケインは、チャンピオンズリーグでアトレティコ・マドリードとの対戦を控える中、バイエルン・ミュンヘンが困難な局面を乗り越える手助けをしたいと決意している。
articles.body:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane expects to sign a new contract with Bayern Munich "within the next few days".

The England captain is heading towards the end of the four-year deal he agreed after leaving Tottenham Hotspur in the summer of 2023.

Kane scored 73 goals for club and country last season, winning two trophies in Germany and leading England to third place at the World Cup.

And the 33-year-old -- who last week was crowned the world's best player at a glittering ceremony in London -- is ready to extend his stay at the Allianz Arena.

"I would say it is more [a matter of] days," Kane said at a news conference ahead of Tuesday's Champions League match at Atlético Madrid. "There has been good conversations over this weekend and today as well.

"I know I keep saying we are close, but we are extremely close now. Details are just details in every contract.

"A lot of the bigger stuff has been ironed out and we are happy with, but in every contract there is loads of little things that go into it, small details that in the end the lawyers have to thrash out and figure out.

"So all in all I would say it is more days than weeks. From what I have heard, the conversations have gone well again today and hopefully we will be in a place to do something within the next few days."

Contract situation aside, Kane also said he is determined to help Bayern Munich come through more difficult moments the have faced this season and, in particular, the "rollercoaster ride" of the past week which saw him crowned the world's best player in London and then miss a penalty against Der Klassiker rivals Borussia Dortmund, in a 2-2 draw at the Allianz.

Bayern's selection problems deepened after the game, with midfielder Ismael Saibari facing a lengthy spell out after needing ankle surgery following his injury and forward Serge Gnabry having sustained a hamstring tear.

Assistant coach Aaron Danks will again take charge in Madrid on Tuesday night as Vincent Kompany continues his recovery at home after being diagnosed with meningeal irritation following his collapse during training.

Bayern will also check on Michael Olise and goalkeeper Manuel Neuer.

Olise picked up a knee problem late on against Dortmund, but trained on Monday. Neuer has also travelled to Spain as he looks to return from a foot injury.

Kane admits it has been a tough spell but one which he feels the Bayern squad can pull through together as they look to push on again following a 2-2 draw with Arsenal in their last European fixture.

"It has been a rollercoaster ride. We have experienced all sorts of emotions," Kane said at a news conference. "I had a fantastic moment winning the Ballon d'Or, but there were also the injuries and Joshua Kimmich's situation [earlier in the season] ... Those were difficult moments.

"You have to be able to cope with that, sport brings us together. We are missing key players and our coach too, but there are others who can seize this opportunity to show what they're made o

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Both Manchester clubs eye move for USMNT's Freeman
articles.description: Several Premier League clubs are interested in signing Villarreal and United States international Alex Freeman. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Manchester United, Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur are all considering a move for United States defender Alex Freeman, while United prospect JJ Gabriel is moving closer to joining Real Madrid. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are all looking at Villarreal and United States' right back Alex Freeman, according to Football Insider. The 22-year-old has caught the eye with a strong 2026, which included him being a regular in Mauricio Pochettino's side at the FIFA World Cup. Spurs are looking for a right back as there is uncertainty surrounding Pedro Porro's future despite the 27-year-old signing a contract extension in the summer.

- Real Madrid are increasingly confident that they can sign Manchester United young attacking midfielder JJ Gabriel, according to TEAMtalk. The 16-year-old has been absent for the Red Devils since requesting to leave in September and asking for his registration to be canceled. Attempts to keep him at Old Trafford have failed so far and a move to Spain has long been seen as the most attractive option, with Real Madrid and Barcelona the leading contenders. There is still competition from Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund.

- Alejandro Balde has accepted that he will need to leave Barcelona if he wants to get more game time, according to Mundo Deportivo. Manchester United and other English clubs are interested in the left-back, who is attracted to the idea of moving to England. Manchester City and Bayern Munich were interested in the 23-year-old during the summer, although the latter went for Nathaniel Brown. Balde is still yet to start a match for the Blaugrana this season with João Cancelo and Xavi Espart ahead of him in the pecking order.
